Container.Name: MediaReducer
Container.Overview: Keeps a large movie library under control on a NAS where the media is the part that gives way. It reads your library from Plex/Tautulli, Jellyfin or both, scores every movie on watch history and IMDb rating, and deletes the lowest-value files first when your storage thresholds are crossed. [br][br] [b]EARLY ALPHA. This app deletes movie files and there is no recycle bin.[/b] It starts paused and deletes nothing. Leave it on Monitor Only and use Simulate until the output is exactly what you would have deleted yourself. Keep backups. [br][br] [b]Do not expose the WebUI to the internet.[/b] There is no login, so anyone who can reach the port can reconfigure it and delete your media. Keep it on your LAN or behind a VPN. Reaching it through a reverse-proxy domain? Put that domain in MEDIAREDUCER_TRUSTED_HOSTS. [br][br] Requires Tautulli (for Plex) or Jellyfin, and internet access for the IMDb ratings dataset. Radarr is optional, for forgetting a movie once its file is gone so it is not re-downloaded.

Config.Name: WebUI Port
Config.Description: Port for the web interface. The container always listens on 7474 internally; change the host side only.

Config.Name: Movie library
Config.Description: The folder that CONTAINS your movie folders, not the movie folder itself. If your films are in /mnt/user/media/Movies, put /mnt/user/media here and add Movies as a monitored path in the UI. Must be writable: this is the only place MediaReducer can delete from.

Config.Name: Config storage
Config.Description: Settings, logs, cache, the IMDb dataset and your deletion history. Keep this on the array so it survives a container rebuild.

Config.Name: Tautulli appdata (optional)
Config.Description: Read-only, and only so Auto Detect can read the Tautulli API key and Plex token out of Tautulli's own config. Skip it and type those in yourself.

Config.Name: Radarr appdata (optional)
Config.Description: Read-only, and only so Auto Detect can read the Radarr API key. Skip it and type the key in yourself. There is no Jellyfin equivalent: Jellyfin issues keys from its own dashboard and stores none on disk.

Config.Name: TZ
Config.Description: Time zone for the daily run time, deletion-delay aging and log timestamps, e.g. America/New_York. Without it the container clock is usually UTC. It can also be set in the UI under Advanced.

Config.Name: PUID
Config.Description: Run as this user instead of root. 99 is nobody on Unraid. That user needs write access to your movie files and to /config, since deletions happen with exactly its permissions. Leave both PUID and PGID blank to run as root.

Config.Name: PGID
Config.Description: Group for the above. 100 is users on Unraid.

Config.Name: MEDIAREDUCER_TRUSTED_HOSTS
Config.Description: Only needed behind a reverse proxy. Comma-separated list of domains you reach the UI on, e.g. media.example.com. Unknown Host headers are rejected as a DNS-rebinding guard, so a proxy domain that is not listed here cannot load the page.
